It serves major Indian and global OEMs across the two-wheeler, three-wheeler and four-wheeler segments from strategically located plants in India and Europe, and is extending into electric-mobility components such as lithium-ion battery packs and into non-automotive …

risks.note: The global economy remains susceptible to renewed trade disruptions and geopolitical escalations; escalating tensions in West Asia could disrupt key energy supply routes and trigger volatility in global oil markets, impacting fuel prices, logistics costs and industrial production.

The industry operates in a dynamic regulatory environment characterised by tightening emission and safety norms and evolving fuel efficiency and Electric Vehicle policies, which drive product re-engineering and compliance investment.
risks.risk: Tightening emission and safety regulation and evolving EV policy

risks.note: Explicitly flagged by the Board as a challenge for the industry alongside the regulatory environment, affecting input availability and cost.
risks.risk: Supply chain constraints and rising compliance costs

risks.note: The Board flags affordability and financing conditions as demand-side pressures; volume growth in FY 2025-26 was itself partly a function of the September 2025 GST rate rationalisation lowering cost of ownership, making demand sensitive to policy support.
risks.risk: Demand-side pressure from affordability and financing conditions

risks.note: The competitive landscape is intensifying with global OEM participation, new EV entrants and increasing focus on technology, localisation and innovation.
risks.risk: Intensifying competition in the auto component landscape

risks.note: A significant minority share of consolidated total income is generated by overseas operations, and European auto sales grew only modestly (about 1.8% year-on-year in FY 2025-26), so Europe remains a slower-growth, macro-exposed part of the portfolio.
New business wins from OEMs in India are reported excluding orders from one of the Company's major OEM customers, indicating a single customer relationship large enough to be disclosed separately.
risks.risk: Concentration on a major OEM customer

risks.note: Accelerating EV adoption, ADAS advancement and record BEV market shares in advanced markets are reshaping the components industry, requiring continuous reinvestment to keep the ICE-linked portfolio relevant.

sk.overview: The industry covers control-intensive, critical-to-the-application electronic control units (ECUs) for the mobility (2/3-wheeler) and industrial (generator/genset) markets. In mobility, ECUs (ISG, EFI, ISG+EFI, EV motor control units) are indispensable to vehicle function; adoption is driven by regulation (emissions/efficiency) and OEM technology transitions, with Tier-I suppliers driving innovation.
